_comment: Tunable weights/costs for compare_benchmarks.py. Lower cost = better. All values are in the same 0-100-ish 'gap points' unit as a MIP gap percentage, so they can be compared directly against a real gap_pct. Edit this file (or pass --weights <file>) to explore how sensitive a ranking is to how harshly you penalize each outcome.
_cost_solved: Proven optimal, or proven infeasible on a genuinely infeasible instance. Best possible outcome.
_gap_cap: Ceiling applied to a real reported/derived MIP gap (%) for TIMEOUT/MEMLIMIT-with-solution instances, so one pathological instance can't dominate the average.
_cost_no_solution: Run stopped (timeout/memlimit) with NO integer-feasible solution ever found/persisted. Strictly worse than the worst possible real gap (gap_cap).
_cost_overtime: Cbc ignored its own -sec/-maxNodes limit and had to be hard-killed by the harness. Worse than cost_no_solution: not only did it fail to solve, it also blew the time budget users asked for.
_cost_error: Run crashed / ASAN error / exited abnormally before producing any parsable result.
_cost_wrong: Validator caught a solver-correctness bug: a claimed-optimal or claimed-infeasible answer that is actually wrong (WRONG_OBJ, INFEASIBLE_WRONG, INVALID_SOL, or a FAIL from cbc_validate_sol). Set far above every other cost by default because this indicates a bug, not just a weaker heuristic result -- it should dominate any ranking.
_cost_unknown: Fallback cost for any status text the loader doesn't recognize (keeps the script from crashing on future/unseen status strings; treated the same as no_solution by default).
_primal_gap_clip: Min/max applied to the primal gap (%) vs BKS before averaging, so one wildly-off instance doesn't dominate the mean.
_dual_gap_clip: Same clipping, applied to the dual gap (%) vs BKS.
_tie_break: How to break ties in average cost when ranking experiments. Currently only 'n_solved_desc' (more confirmed-optimal/infeasible wins) is implemented.
